Uninterrupted uniaxial tensile tests were conducted to capture the macroscopic mechanical behaviors. The Q&P steel exhibits a yield strength of 1196 MPa, an ultimate strength of 1447 MPa and an elongation of 40.0%, while the Q&T steel exhibits a yield strength of 1465 MPa, an ultimate strength of 1952 MPa and an elongation of 23.6% (Supplementary Fig. S1). In contrast, interrupted uniaxial tensile tests were performed to investigate the microscopic strain distribution and void evolution on the surface. HR-DIC was utilized to reveal the strain distribution at the nanoscale. The DIC patterns were generated by remodeling a 5 nm thick Au layer sputtered on the specimen surface using water vapors  [17,39] . Backscattered electron images (BSE, JSM-7900F, JEOL, Japan, acceleration voltage: 15 kV, working distance: 4 mm, probe current: No. 8), captured at 15000
